segments.summary: The interviewee, originally from Morocco, studied industrial engineering at Northeastern University, completed internships in tech and consulting, and aspires to launch an edtech company in Morocco while also performing magic tricks.
The interviewee cites exposure to strategic projects and opportunities for externships, particularly in education, as key reasons for joining the consulting firm.
The interviewee successfully sourced and negotiated with a South Korean supplier for generators, saving 10% on the project cost while launching a new department at an electrical power plant.
The interviewee identified persuasion and leadership as their two biggest strengths.

The interviewee convinced the vice president of supply chain to avoid delaying a major Amazon robotic facility launch by sourcing unused materials from existing facilities instead of waiting for delayed Japanese supplies.

The interviewee described leading a real estate occupancy project at Boston Consulting Group, where they automated data processes, collaborated with a team of 15 developers, and created a Tableau dashboard that satisfied partners, gaining managerial experience.
The interviewee identifies prioritization as a key challenge but has improved by seeking guidance from their manager to align tasks with business priorities.
The interviewee asked how the consulting business model might adapt to remote work and what the company's major goals, such as international expansion, are for 2025.
